text:
Micah: quick thread — we need a concrete per-org rate policy that mixes RPM/TPM with a concurrency cap. proposing we standardize semantics before shipping UI changes.

Tanya: +1. do we want RPM (requests/min) or TPM (tokens/min) to be the primary knob? they behave very differently under tiny vs huge requests.

Micah: leaning to TPM primary for cost-aligned billing, RPM as a secondary safeguard. concurrency cap enforced separately to protect runtime.

Simon: TPM primary makes sense, but we must handle small-request noise. lots of tiny calls can spike concurrency without burning many tokens. need a hybrid enforcement at router + runtime.

Alex: UX ask — console should show "effective limits" (TPM, RPM, concurrency) and an example workload simulator (requests/sec, avg tokens) so users can see throttles before saving.

Tanya: +1 to simulator. also need an explanatory tooltip: "TPM counts prompt+completion tokens; RPM counts requests. concurrency is active inflight requests."

Micah: ops question: where do we enforce? edge LB (fast reject), or router (better visibility), or runtime (accurate tokens)?

Simon: prefer multi-layer: quick edge checks for RPM/concurrency fast rejects, router for TPM estimation (prefix caching awareness), runtime for final token accounting and exact rejections. fallback path if runtime disagrees.

Micah: telemetry requirements then: per-org token_consumed, req_count, inflight_peak, throttled_count, avg_latency_p95, throttle_reason (rpm|tpm|concurrency).

Tanya: + add histograms for refill windows and burst_credit_balance. we also want alerting: spike in throttled_count OR sudden change in inflight_peak.

Alex: for rollout UX: allow "preview mode" where console simulates throttles but does not enforce (logs only), then canary enforce for a subset of orgs. we need a button: "simulate for X orgs".

Simon: edge case: orgs that pin dedicated capacity or Dedicated customers should have different defaults and skip soft throttling. document that.

Micah: policy model idea (config snippet):
```yaml
policy:
  primary_limit:
    unit: tokens
    window: 60s
    amount: 120000  # TPM
  secondary_limit:
    unit: requests
    window: 60s
    amount: 3000    # RPM fallback
  concurrency_cap: 200
  burst_credits:
    capacity: 10000
    refill_per_min: 2000
  enforcement:
    edge: fast_reject(rpm, concurrency)
    router: precheck(tpm_estimate)
    runtime: authoritative(token_count)
  fallback_policy: degrade->queue->reject
```

Tanya: nice. question: what should burst_credits be charged against? tokens or requests? I think tokens.

Simon: tokens. also implement a grace window for sudden traffic increases: allow utilization to exceed TPM by drawing down burst_credits but throttle when burst is exhausted.

Alex: console needs to indicate current burst balance and projected minutes until refill at current usage. small UI widgets.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rate-policy-service v2 will include burst accounting metrics (will post prod links after deploy). :gear:

Micah: testing plan:
- unit tests for token accounting
- integration sim with mixed small/large requests
- chaos tests where router and runtime disagree to verify fallback logging
- telemetry dashboards (per-org) and alert rules

Tanya: also add e2e for console simulator accuracy vs real enforcement. show differences in a "why I was throttled" modal with last 10 calls.

Simon: opt-in beta orgs: pick 10 active orgs across tiers to validate. schedule migration window and a rollback plan.

Micah: Action items:
- Simon: design router quick-check logic and failure modes.
- Alex: wireframe effective-limits + simulator + burst widget.
- Tanya: list telemetry metrics + alert thresholds.
- Micah: write rollout plan and canary criteria.

Micah: thanks all. if anyone has vetoes on TPM primary, say now. otherwise i'll start drafting the RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
